auth_methods.quote: Whether you’re handling OAuth 2.0, verifying requests, or setting up Sign in with Slack, we’ve got you covered.
auth_methods.note: Bot/user/app tokens (xoxb-/xoxp-/xapp-) are sent as Bearer; obtained via OAuth 2.0 install.

credential_access.quote: Every developer enrolled in the Slack Developer Program is eligible to provision a basic sandbox.
credential_access.note: Free workspace or free sandbox, app created self-serve at api.slack.com/apps.

production_gate.note: Two readings. (1) none: apps can be distributed ('unlisted') without Marketplace listing. (2) marketplace_listing: non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps get conversations.history/replies limited to 1 request/min and 15 objects for new installs; Marketplace review requires 10+ active workspace installs. Best guess: none for installability, with serious rate-limit penalty.

api_type.note: Two readings. Docs state the Web API is 'HTTP RPC-style methods' and 'not a REST API', and also offer Socket Mode/Events API (websocket/HTTP). Best guess: rpc_websocket; a labeller treating HTTP JSON as rest would say rest.

mcp_official.quote: With the Slack MCP server, your integrated apps can search channels, send messages, and perform other Slack actions through MCP clients.
mcp_official.note: Hosted by Slack; workspace admin approval for clients.

main_blocker_type.quote: The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request.
main_blocker_type.note: Biggest obstacle for a multi-tenant toolkit is rate limiting of unlisted apps (history/replies) unless Marketplace-approved. Could also be read as commercial/none.
